newsitem.title: HUNGARY: New Hungary poll keeps governing Socialists ahead.
newsitem.headline: New Hungary poll keeps governing Socialists ahead.

text.p: Hungary's senior governing party, the Socialists, have maintained their lead in the opinion polls, although half the population is undecided, according to a survey published on Saturday.

The poll, carried out by the Hungarian firm Szazadveg-TARKI for the daily Magyar Hirlap, gave the Socialist Party (MSZP) 32 percent while the opposition parties the Federation of Young Democrats (Fidesz) and the Independent Smallholders (FKGP) scored 26 and 21 percent respectively.
However, 50 percent of those polled had not yet made up their minds ahead of elections due to be held in May 1998.

Two polls published at the end of June put the Socialists, led by Prime Minister Gyula Horn, clearly ahead for the first time this year, one giving them a lead of three points and the other an eight-point margin.
Analysts at the time to positive signs in the economy and an expected invitation for Hungary to join NATO.
Since then Hungary has received its NATO invitation and has been named by the European Commission in the first group of countries it recommends for early talks on accession to the European Union.
The Socialists' junior coalition partner, the Alliance of Free Democrats, scored nine percent, the same as in June.
The two parties together gained around 53 percent of the popular vote in the 1994 election, giving them 72 percent of seats in Parliament.
